content: Glimepiride is an oral hypoglycemic medication that has been associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular mortality. It is essential to discuss the potential risks, benefits, and alternative treatments with your doctor before starting this medication. Glimepiride is prescribed to manage type 2 diabetes, a condition where the body does not use insulin effectively, leading to poor blood sugar control. This medication works by stimulating the pancreas to produce more insulin and increasing the body’s sensitivity to insulin. It can be used with or without insulin. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Glimepiride is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once daily. It should be consumed with breakfast or the first substantial meal of the day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking glimepiride even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Before taking glimepiride, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to glimepiride or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially antibiotics, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), dexamethasone, diuretics, estrogens, isoniazid, MAO inhibitors, medications for high blood pressure or heart disease, niacin, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, prednisone, probenecid, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney disease or diabetic ketoacidosis. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor immediately. If you become pregnant while taking glimepiride, contact your doctor right away. Additionally, if you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking glimepiride. Follow all dietary and exercise recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. Maintain a healthy diet. Alcohol consumption can lower blood sugar levels, so consult your doctor about the safe use of alcoholic beverages while on this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If you will be eating a snack soon, take the dose with the snack. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Glimepiride may cause changes in blood sugar levels. Be aware of the symptoms of both low and high blood sugar and know how to respond. Hypoglycemia (low blood sugar) is a potential side effect of this medication. Your doctor will provide instructions on managing hypoglycemia, which may include checking your blood sugar, consuming sugary foods or drinks (e.g., hard candy or fruit juice), or seeking medical care. Symptoms of hypoglycemia include shakiness, dizziness, sweating, nervousness, irritability, sudden mood changes, headache, numbness or tingling around the mouth, weakness, pale skin, hunger, and clumsy or jerky movements. If untreated, severe symptoms such as confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness may occur. Ensure that family, friends, and others around you are aware of these symptoms and know to seek immediate medical attention if necessary. Hyperglycemia (high blood sugar) can also occur. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience extreme thirst, frequent urination, extreme hunger, weakness, or blurred vision. Untreated hyperglycemia can lead to diabetic ketoacidosis, a life-threatening condition. Symptoms of diabetic ketoacidosis include dry mouth, upset stomach, vomiting, shortness of breath, fruity-smelling breath, and decreased consciousness. Seek medical attention immediately if you experience these symptoms. Store glimepiride in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unused medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order tests to monitor your response to glimepiride and may instruct you on how to check your blood or urine sugar levels at home. Always wear a diabetic identification bracelet to ensure proper treatment in emergencies. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
